attacks.claim: Rollback after the remainder send re-enables MailPoet without reverse-syncing unsubscribes, bounces, complaints, or paid-status changes made in Ghost. MailPoet could then re-mail people who opted out during the Ghost window, which cannot be undone.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet." ABSENT: reverse-sync of Ghost-side unsubscribes, bounces, complaints, and paid status.

attacks.claim: Spam-complaint status is not in the MailPoet export spec, so complaint suppressions may be dropped at import. Complaints are the most sensitive suppression category and the main driver of sender reputation.
attacks.evidence: "Export MailPoet subscribers with status, list membership, subscribe date, and consent source/IP where recorded." vs. "Unsubscribed and bounced addresses are imported as suppressed." ABSENT: complaint/spam-report mapping.

attacks.claim: The 37 mismatched paid members have no named owner, deadline, or post-import check that each maps to exactly one Stripe subscription and one Ghost member. Risks double billing or lost paid access at cutover.
attacks.evidence: "37 members with mismatched emails were identified in a dry run and will be resolved by hand before cutover." ABSENT: owner, deadline, verification step.

attacks.claim: The production subscriber and member import has no explicit timeline slot. Cutover depends on it, but the schedule lists only staging dry runs and reconciliation.
attacks.evidence: "Dry-run import on staging in week 1 ... before the production import." Week 3 and week 4 entries contain no production import step.

attacks.claim: The go/no-go rule for the 2,000-to-46k remainder send is ambiguous. It does not say what happens if bounce or complaint data is missing or lagging at the 2-hour mark, or who makes the call.
attacks.evidence: "the remainder sends 2 hours later if bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1%" ABSENT: behaviour when metrics are unavailable; named decision owner.

attacks.claim: Mailgun domain warm-up is a single week-2 DNS task with no volume ramp. A 2,000-address seed followed two hours later by 46k on a new sending domain risks throttling or reputation damage with no evidence it is survivable.
attacks.evidence: "Mailgun domain warm-up (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)" in week 2; "First Ghost send goes to a 2,000-subscriber seed segment" ABSENT: volume ramp schedule.

attacks.claim: Send-path capacity at 46k recipients is untested. The only send rehearsal is 50 addresses, so the 'zero send-day outages' target has no evidence behind it.
attacks.evidence: "rehearse this end to end with a 50-address internal list through Postmark Broadcasts" ABSENT: staging send or load test at approximately 46,000 recipients.

attacks.claim: Ghost, MySQL, and bulk sending share one 8 GB box, the same single-host topology behind the four send-day outages. Backups allow up to 24 hours of data loss, and no RTO, failover, or send-path alerting is defined.
attacks.evidence: "MySQL 8 on the same box, nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)." ABSENT: RTO, failover target, send-failure and dump-failure alerting.

attacks.claim: Mailgun receives recipient batches, but no DPA is referenced before the domain is switched on. Consent IPs have no stated retention rule in the live table, and weekly export copies have no deletion path.
attacks.evidence: "Mailgun only receives per-send recipient batches." and "consent source/IP where recorded" and "stored with the DB dumps" ABSENT: DPA reference, consent-IP retention period, export deletion path.

attacks.claim: Member exports with consent IPs and Stripe IDs sit beside DB dumps in object storage, with no stated bucket access policy, key management, or handling for Mailgun, Stripe, and SMTP credentials.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)" and "stored with the DB dumps" ABSENT: key management, bucket access policy, secrets handling.

attacks.claim: Importing 46,000 active subscribers with their consent records assumes consent continuity across the platform change. No legal review of that basis is planned, and suppressing opt-outs alone does not establish it.
attacks.evidence: "never as active, so nobody who opted out is re-mailed" and "consent source/IP where recorded" ABSENT: legal basis or consent-continuity review for the active import.

attacks.claim: One 0.5 FTE developer owns VPS build, backups, migration, shortcode fixes, theme port, redirects, Stripe reconciliation, Mailgun warm-up, and editor training in four weeks, with no named backup owner for the cutover window.
The exit path rehearses only with 50 addresses through Postmark, which is absent from the cost model. Throughput and reputation transfer for a 46k list to a second sender are unmeasured.
attacks.evidence: "rehearse this end to end with a 50-address internal list through Postmark Broadcasts" (no Postmark line in "Total run cost: ~$140/mo").

attacks.claim: The $90 Mailgun figure has no stated rate or tier basis, and storage is unquantified. The components sum to about $138 before storage, so the total is consistent but unsourced.
attacks.evidence: "Estimated $90/mo at our volume (46k x ~4.3 sends/month)." and "Total run cost: ~$140/mo VPS + Mailgun + storage"

attacks.claim: Ghost is pinned only to a major version range, and native Stripe support is asserted without a tested configuration on the proposed VPS.
attacks.evidence: "Ghost 5.x (MIT licensed) self-hosted via the official Docker image" ABSENT: pinned version and Stripe test.

attacks.claim: Success measures omit reader-facing regression metrics such as open, click, unsubscribe, and paid conversion, so migration harm to readers would not be detected.
attacks.evidence: "Zero send-day outages over the first quarter." ABSENT: reader KPIs and thresholds.

attacks.claim: Editors are trained in week 3 and have only two days on the production tool before the first Ghost send.
attacks.evidence: "editor training" in week 3 and "giving 2 days to fix issues before the first Ghost send."

attacks.claim: The theme port has no visual or accessibility acceptance check for the top URLs before cutover.
attacks.evidence: "theme port" in week 2 ABSENT: rendered-page and accessibility acceptance criteria.

attacks.claim: Only the 2,000 most-visited URLs are crawl-verified, out of roughly 6,812 posts plus category and tag redirects. The remaining archive is unchecked.
attacks.evidence: "A crawl of the 2,000 most-visited URLs from analytics must return 200/301 before cutover."
